_: Zone programs that are KNOWN red, and the exact diagnostic codes each must fail with.
This file INVERTS an assertion; it never removes one. A recorded program is still
expanded and still judged, and three things are findings: it passes (the record has
expired), it fails with a different code (a second defect was hiding behind the first),
or it fails with one more. A plain skip would be satisfied by the very defect it
excuses, which is the vacuity mode this project has shipped six times.
Every entry below has ONE cause. An orientation-sensitive block state cannot be a
palette role: a role binds one state to one name, and a connection, facing or rotation
property names a WORLD direction that a reorientation does not rewrite. So a zone that
wants bars or a mounted skull has two moves and both are red. Leave the role bare and
the state omits its connections (DW0735 isolated post, DW0737 under-specified); write
the connections into the role and the state lands turned wherever the scope turned
(DW0736). z3/z4/z6 took the first horn and z1/z2 took the second, which is why the
same gap shows up under three different codes.
The mechanism that DOES express it — one alternative per orientation under a
`Cond::Orientation` guard, carrying the state that matches — is inline-only, so
reaching for it costs the campaign the role surface it restyles the material through.
grammar.md names the missing surface (an oriented palette role) as a gap. Closing it is
engine work, and until it lands these five zones stay recorded here rather than being
hand-turned by whoever notices, because which way a bar faces is a design decision.
